title_en: Jiangsu Consumer Rights Protection Committee v. Lerong Zhixin Electronic Technology (Tianjin) Co., Ltd. — civil public interest litigation for consumer rights
ruling_gist_en: When a smart TV is turned on, the startup advertisement plays automatically. If the smart TV producer is also the operator of the startup advertisement, it has the obligation to clearly inform consumers that the product contains a startup advertisement and to inform them whether the advertisement can be turned off with one click. Where a smart TV producer fails to provide an instant one-click close function for the smart TVs it produces and sells, and a consumer rights protection organization, for the purpose of protecting the legitimate rights and interests of numerous unspecified consumers, initiates a civil public interest lawsuit requesting the smart TV producer to provide a one-click close function for the startup advertisement, the people's court shall support the claim.

full_text_en:
Jiangsu Provincial Consumer Rights Protection Commission v. Lerong Zhixin Electronic Technology (Tianjin) Co., Ltd. — public interest consumer civil litigation

[Ruling Summary]

When a smart TV is turned on and an advertisement automatically plays during startup, if the smart TV manufacturer is also the operator of such startup advertisements, it has an obligation to clearly inform consumers that the product contains startup advertisements and to disclose whether there is an option to close them with one click. Where a smart TV manufacturer fails to provide an immediate one-click close function for startup advertisements on the smart TVs it produces and sells, and a consumer rights protection organization, in order to protect the legitimate rights and interests of numerous unspecified consumers, initiates a civil public interest lawsuit demanding that the smart TV manufacturer provide a one-click close function for startup advertisements, the people's court shall support such a claim.

Plaintiff: Jiangsu Provincial Consumer Rights Protection Commission, domiciled at Beijing West Road, Gulou District, Nanjing, Jiangsu Province.
Legal Representative: Lu Xichun, Secretary-General of the Commission.

Defendant: Lerong Zhixin Electronic Technology (Tianjin) Co., Ltd., domiciled at Middle Animation Road, Tianjin Eco-City, Tianjin.
Legal Representative: Mao Binglong, Manager of the Company.

The plaintiff, Jiangsu Provincial Consumer Rights Protection Commission (hereinafter referred to as the Jiangsu Provincial Consumer Rights Protection Commission), initiated a public interest consumer civil litigation dispute against the defendant, Lerong Zhixin Electronic Technology (Tianjin) Co., Ltd. (hereinafter referred to as Lerong Zhixin Company), and filed a lawsuit with the Nanjing Intermediate People's Court.

Plaintiff's Allegations: Based on consumer complaints, the plaintiff's investigation revealed that the defendant had installed a startup advertisement function in its branded smart TV products sold. Upon turning on the smart TV, consumers would automatically view a startup advertisement lasting approximately 15 seconds, but the defendant did not notify consumers at the time of sale of such advertisements, nor could the advertisements be closed. Consumers generally reported that the startup advertisements diminished their television viewing experience. In response to consumer complaints, the plaintiff conducted a questionnaire survey and, based on the results, sent a rectification notice to the defendant and collectively summoned smart TV operators, including the defendant, for talks. After the collective talks, most smart TV operators were able to rectify the issue, but the defendant did not actively do so. The defendant, without obtaining consumer consent, sent advertisements through internet-connected smart TVs and failed to provide a one-click close function, thereby violating Articles 43 and 44 of the *Advertising Law of the People's Republic of China* and Articles 8, 9, and 10 of the *Law of the People's Republic of China on the Protection of Consumer Rights and Interests*, infringing on consumers' rights to be informed, to choose, and to fair dealing. The plaintiff, as a consumer rights protection organization, lawfully initiated a public interest lawsuit and requested a judgment ordering the following: 1. The defendant shall, in a conspicuous manner, prompt or inform consumers when selling smart TVs with a startup advertisement function that such advertisements exist in the product; 2. The defendant shall provide a one-click close function for startup advertisements on its smart TVs sold with such a function; 3. The defendant shall bear the litigation costs of this case.

Defendant's Defense: 1. Regarding the obligation to inform before sale: After the plaintiff's collective talks, the defendant clearly informed consumers of the existence of startup advertisements on the product introduction pages of online sales platforms, including but not limited to JD.com, for various models of Letv smart TVs. Consumers have full right to know before purchase. The product detail page includes a prompt stating: "This TV contains power-on/off advertisements, but you can upload custom startup videos. Detailed steps, please consult customer service." The product manual also informs on the after-sales service support page, the purchase agreement on the Letv Mall website clearly states it, and the product outer packaging also clearly indicates it, ensuring that consumers are aware at the time of purchase. 2. Regarding safeguarding consumers' right to choose: After the rectification following the talks, the defendant had already provided a customized video function to offer differentiated services based on consumer needs. 3. Regarding the one-click close function for startup advertisements: The defendant had completed rectification. The defendant had already developed a one-click close function and was in the stage of debugging the stability of hardware and software adaptation for various models. 4. Regarding the display of startup advertisements: The defendant's TV products comply with national and industry standards. To optimize the boring waiting time during startup, users can watch fine advertisements or contact the defendant's customer service to customize startup videos. These startup screens do not affect users' normal use of the product, nor do they occupy users' effective time. The legislative purpose of Article 44 of the *Advertising Law of the People's Republic of China* is to "not affect users' normal use of the network," and the law does not prohibit all internet advertisements. In summary, due to technical reasons, the defendant's products sold have a certain startup waiting time. Playing advertisements during this time does not infringe on consumer rights, as sufficient information was provided at the time of sale, and consumers can customize changes to the startup advertisements, fully protecting consumers' rights to be informed and to choose. The law does not mandatorily require the cancellation of startup advertisements, but the defendant still rectified the issue and hopes to reach a settlement with the plaintiff to create a favorable business environment. The defendant undertakes to set a one-click close function for its TVs containing startup advertisements, in compliance with laws, regulations, and rules, with execution standards not lower than mainstream models on the market. Although rectification was made, this does not mean the defendant has violated the law. If a settlement cannot be reached, the defendant respectfully requests the court to dismiss the lawsuit according to law and protect the defendant's legitimate rights and interests.

Facts Found by the Nanjing Intermediate People's Court at First Instance:

The defendant, Lerong Zhixin Company, is the operator of branded smart TVs such as "LeEco TV," "Letv," and "Letv Super TV." On March 16, 2019, the plaintiff, the Jiangsu Provincial Consumer Rights Protection Commission, received a complaint from a consumer in Nanjing, reporting that the smart TVs sold by the defendant had startup advertisements that could not be closed.

After receiving the consumer complaint, the plaintiff performed the following public interest duties: 1. Accepted the complaint and conducted an investigation. During the investigation, the plaintiff found that when a smart TV sold by the defendant was turned on, a startup advertisement automatically played for approximately 15 seconds; the defendant did not conspicuously prompt or inform consumers of the existence of startup advertisements at the time of sale, nor could the advertisements be closed. In response to consumer complaints, the plaintiff conducted a questionnaire survey. Consumers left messages stating they could not accept startup advertisements on smart TVs and that such advertisements infringed their rights. 2. Based on the investigation results, the plaintiff collectively summoned smart TV operators, including the defendant, for talks and sent a rectification notice to the defendant. On September 4, 2019, the plaintiff sent a "Letter on the Issue of Infringement of Consumer Rights by Smart TV Startup Advertisements" to smart TV operators, including the defendant. On October 10, 2019, the plaintiff collectively summoned seven major brand smart TV operators with high market share, including the defendant, to inform them that smart TV startup advertisements infringed consumers' rights to be informed, to choose, and to fair dealing. On the same day, the plaintiff sent a "Notice to Enterprises" to the defendant, requesting that the defendant inform consumers of the existence of startup advertisements when selling smart TVs and provide consumers with a one-click close function for startup advertisements, fulfilling legal obligations to protect consumers' rights to be informed, to choose, and to fair dealing, and to improve complaint handling mechanisms. 3. Initiated this public interest lawsuit. After the collective talks, most smart TV manufacturers successively sent rectification response letters to the plaintiff. The plaintiff believed that these manufacturers had technically resolved the issue of one-click close for startup advertisements. The defendant sent a letter to the plaintiff on September 20, 2019, responding to the issues raised in the talk letter, and again on October 21, 2019, making commitments and guarantees regarding the TV startup service. The plaintiff believed that most smart TV operators were able to rectify the issue, but the defendant did not actively do so. As a legally established consumer rights protection organization, the plaintiff, pursuant to Article 55 of the *Civil Procedure Law of the People's Republic of China*, initiated a public interest lawsuit to protect the legitimate rights and interests of numerous unspecified consumers.

During the first-instance trial, the defendant, Lerong Zhixin Company, argued that during the startup warm-up phase, the TV completely could not play television content, and without advertisements, it would be a black screen. Therefore, advertisements or other user-customized videos during this standby period did not affect users' viewing of television.

To prove that startup advertisements are not an essential function of smart TVs, the plaintiff, the Jiangsu Provincial Consumer Rights Protection Commission, submitted a *Test Report* and applied for a person with specialized knowledge, Sun Guozi, to appear in court to testify that technically, when a smart TV starts up, it can simultaneously play advertisements and allow one-click closure. Sun Guozi issued an *Expert Opinion* and stated: 1. Playing advertisements during startup is not a necessary procedure for starting a smart TV. 2. Playing startup advertisements prolongs startup time and increases consumers' waiting time. 3. Smart TV startup advertisements need to use the internet to download updated content. 4. From a technical feasibility perspective, a one-click close function can be provided while playing startup advertisements, allowing consumers to immediately close the advertisement by pressing the close button.

Regarding the specific time for providing the one-click close function for startup advertisements, the defendant, Lerong Zhixin Company, stated that it had already provided a one-click close function, which appeared when 5 seconds remained in a 15-second startup advertisement. The plaintiff, the Jiangsu Provincial Consumer Rights Protection Commission, argued that its claim was to require the defendant to provide a one-click close function simultaneously with the playing of the startup advertisement, i.e., allowing immediate and anytime closure during the advertisement.

It was also found that the plaintiff, the Jiangsu Provincial Consumer Rights Protection Commission, was established on September 13, 2017, with the approval of the Jiangsu Provincial People's Government, replacing the former "Jiangsu Provincial Consumers' Association" to perform the public interest duties granted by the *Law of the People's Republic of China on the Protection of Consumer Rights and Interests*. After accepting the case on January 2, 2020, the first-instance court published a notice of acceptance of this case, but no competent authority or social organization applied to participate in this lawsuit before the trial.

It was further found that during the first instance, the defendant, Lerong Zhixin Company, implemented rectifications for the startup advertisements on its smart TVs, providing prompts regarding the startup advertisement business on the outer packaging and enlarging the prompt font.

The Nanjing Intermediate People's Court held at first instance:

The dispute focus of this case was: Whether the defendant, Lerong Zhixin Company, should provide a one-click close function simultaneously with the playing of startup advertisements on the smart TVs it sells; whether it infringed consumers' legitimate rights such as the right to be informed and to choose; and whether it should bear corresponding civil liability.

Consumers have the right to freely choose goods or services. Consumers have the right to fair dealing. Article 43, Paragraph 1 of the *Advertising Law of the People's Republic of China* provides: "No unit or individual may, without the consent or request of the party concerned, send advertisements to their residences, means of transport, etc., or send advertisements by means of electronic information." Article 44 provides: "The use of the internet for advertising activities shall be governed by the provisions of this Law. The use of the internet to publish or send advertisements shall not affect users' normal use of the network. Advertisements published by means of pop-ups or other forms on internet pages shall prominently display a close mark and ensure one-click closure." In this case, the plaintiff, the Jiangsu Provincial Consumer Rights Protection Commission, as a legally established organization, performs the duties of a consumers' association, conducting social supervision over goods and services, accepting consumer complaints, and protecting consumer rights. Pursuant to Article 55 of the *Civil Procedure Law of the People's Republic of China*, Article 47 of the *Law of the People's Republic of China on the Protection of Consumer Rights and Interests*, and Article 1 of the *Interpretation of the Supreme People's Court on Several Issues Concerning the Application of Law in the Trial of Consumer Civil Public Interest Litigation Cases*, it has the right to initiate this lawsuit. The defendant, Lerong Zhixin Company, loaded startup advertisements on the branded smart TVs it produced and sold, such as "LeEco TV," "Letv," and "Letv Super TV," and continuously updated the advertisement content via the internet. Consumers, upon startup, automatically viewed a startup advertisement for approximately 15 seconds, and only when 5 seconds remained did a one-click close window pop up, allowing consumers to choose to close the advertisement. This infringed on consumers' right to choose, reduced the experience of watching television, and infringed on the legitimate rights and interests of numerous unspecified consumers. Moreover, from a technical perspective, playing advertisements during the startup period of a smart TV can fully achieve providing a one-click close function while playing the advertisement. The defendant's defense that the TV requires warm-up waiting during startup and that not playing advertisements would result in a black screen was inconsistent with the facts and not accepted. The plaintiff's request that the defendant provide a one-click close function for startup advertisements simultaneously with their playing on smart TVs sold with such advertisements had factual and legal basis and was supported. Considering the older models previously sold by the defendant, which are limited by hardware and software technology and require significant functional modifications, no time limit for rectification was imposed for smart TVs already sold. The defendant shall, from the effective date of this judgment, provide a one-click close function for startup advertisements simultaneously with their playing on smart TVs sold with a startup advertisement function.

Regarding the plaintiff's request that the defendant conspicuously prompt or inform consumers of the existence of startup advertisements when selling smart TVs, given that the defendant had already rectified this issue, providing corresponding information on the product sales page, in the product manual, in the purchase agreement on the Letv Mall website, and on the product outer packaging with enlarged font prompts, the defendant had essentially fulfilled its obligation to inform consumers of the existence of startup advertisements when selling smart TVs. This claim by the plaintiff was not supported. In summary, part of the plaintiff's claims had factual and legal basis and were supported.

Accordingly, the Nanjing Intermediate People's Court, in accordance with Articles 9, 10, and 47 of the *Law of the People's Republic of China on the Protection of Consumer Rights and Interests*, Articles 43, Paragraph 1, and 44 of the *Advertising Law of the People's Republic of China*, Articles 1, 4, and 13, Paragraph 1 of the *Interpretation of the Supreme People's Court on Several Issues Concerning the Application of Law in the Trial of Consumer Civil Public Interest Litigation Cases*, and Article 55 of the *Civil Procedure Law of the People's Republic of China*, rendered the following judgment on November 10, 2020:

1. The defendant, Lerong Zhixin Electronic Technology (Tianjin) Co., Ltd., shall, from the effective date of this judgment, provide a one-click close function for startup advertisements simultaneously with their playing on smart TVs sold with a startup advertisement function;
2. Reject the other claims of the plaintiff, the Jiangsu Provincial Consumer Rights Protection Commission.

After the first-instance judgment was pronounced, Lerong Zhixin Company, dissatisfied with the judgment, appealed to the Jiangsu High People's Court.

Lerong Zhixin Company's Appeal Arguments: 1. The appellant provided consumers with the option to set family photos, travel photos, etc., as startup videos or to watch television advertisements, and also provided a one-click close function, which fully protected consumers' right to choose. The first-instance court failed to address this and erroneously found that the appellant infringed consumer rights based on the feasibility of setting a one-click close function; 2. Article 43 of the *Advertising Law of the People's Republic of China* clearly lags behind actual social life circumstances. The first-instance court ignored the development status and objective circumstances of the smart TV industry, applying the provision too harshly to the appellant, resulting in a serious imbalance of interests, constituting an error in the application of law. In summary, the appellant requested that the first-instance judgment be revoked and that all claims of the appellee, the Jiangsu Provincial Consumer Rights Protection Commission, be dismissed.

Appellee's Defense: 1. Startup advertisements are not an essential function of TVs. Pursuant to Article 44 of the *Advertising Law of the People's Republic of China*, the appellant, Lerong Zhixin Company, has an obligation to provide a one-click close function for startup advertisements simultaneously with their playing on the smart TVs it sells, ensuring consumers' right to choose whether to watch the advertisements or not; 2. The claim of the Jiangsu Provincial Consumer Rights Protection Commission was to require the appellant to set a one-click close function on its TVs, not other functions. The first-instance court did not need to investigate or address the issues of uploading photos or videos; 3. Setting a one-click close function is to protect consumers' right to choose, not to prohibit the playing of startup advertisements, nor does it harm the appellant's business interests. In summary, the first-instance court correctly found the facts and correctly applied the law. The appellee requested that the appellant's appeal be dismissed.

The Jiangsu High People's Court, upon second-instance trial, confirmed the facts found at first instance.

The Jiangsu High People's Court held at second instance that the dispute focus of this case was: 1. Whether the optional services provided by the appellant, Lerong Zhixin Company, to consumers during the playing of startup advertisements on its smart TVs limited consumers' right to choose; 2. Whether the one-click close function provided by Lerong Zhixin Company complied with the provisions of the *Advertising Law* and other laws.

The court held that startup advertisements are advertisements that are played automatically when a user turns on a smart TV, using the built-in program of the smart TV to download updated content via the internet. The smart TV manufacturer has the right to decide the content and playback mode of the startup advertisements. Therefore, the smart TV manufacturer is also the operator of the startup advertisements. This case is a dispute arising from startup advertisement issues encountered by consumers who purchased TVs produced by the appellant, Lerong Zhixin Company. Consumers' right to freely choose refers to the right of consumers to freely choose or refuse specific goods or services according to their own wishes. Given the dual identity of Lerong Zhixin Company, compared to traditional consumer disputes, the consumers' right to choose in this case has a richer connotation. Whether the right to choose has been infringed should be discussed in two levels. The first level is whether Lerong Zhixin Company fully informed consumers of the startup advertisement situation when they purchased the TV, enabling consumers to fully understand relevant information and freely choose whether to buy or not buy the TV; the second level is whether, when the TV played the startup advertisement, a one-click close function was set in accordance with legal provisions, ensuring that consumers have the right to refuse to receive startup advertisements.

(I) On Whether the Appellant, Lerong Zhixin Company, Infringed Consumers' Right to Choose Whether to Purchase the TV

According to the facts found at first instance, after rectification, the appellant, Lerong Zhixin Company, provided prompts regarding startup advertisements on the product sales page, product manual, purchase agreement on the Letv Mall website, and product outer packaging, with enlarged prompt fonts. In terms of content, Lerong Zhixin Company indicated that startup advertisements would appear when the TV was turned on, and some model packaging also stated that startup advertisements could be replaced by setting photos, videos, etc. Under normal circumstances, this is unlikely to cause consumer misunderstanding, thus safeguarding consumers' right to choose when purchasing a TV. However, it should be noted that the appellant's expression in the relevant prompts regarding whether consumers can close startup advertisements with one click was not clear enough and still requires further improvement. Taking into account the overall circumstances of the case, the first-instance court correctly held that Lerong Zhixin Company had essentially fulfilled its obligation to inform consumers of the existence of startup advertisements when selling smart TVs, which was supported.

(II) On Whether the Appellant, Lerong Zhixin Company, Infringed Consumers' Right to Choose Whether to Watch the Startup Advertisements

Article 29, Paragraph 3 of the *Law of the People's Republic of China on the Protection of Consumer Rights and Interests* provides that "business operators shall not send commercial information to consumers without their consent or request, or if the consumer has expressly refused." Article 44, Paragraph 2 of the *Advertising Law of the People's Republic of China* provides: "When using the Internet to publish or send advertisements, the advertisements shall not affect the normal use of the network by users. Advertisements published on an Internet page in the form of pop-ups or the like shall prominently indicate a close mark to ensure one-click closure." It is thus evident that the law does not prohibit advertising operators from pushing advertisements or other commercial information to consumers through the Internet or other means, but they shall guarantee the consumer's right to refuse (right to choose). The above provisions have fully considered the characteristics of the Internet, balancing the commercial interests of advertising operators, the interests of information circulation, and consumer rights. The consumer's right to choose whether to receive commercial information is a right based on their own will without any need to provide reasons. Setting up a one-click close window in a prominent manner is the statutory form to ensure the realization of this right, and it is also an unconditional statutory obligation to be undertaken by the business operator. This statutory obligation shall be immediate and thorough. Only when the close window appears simultaneously with the Internet advertisement and can completely close the advertisement can the consumer's right to choose be fully protected, and can the normative purpose of the law — "to ensure one-click closure" and "not to affect the normal use of the network by users" — be achieved.

In this case, the smart televisions sold by the appellant, Lerong Zhixin Company, provided consumers with the function of setting startup photos or videos. However, this function only granted consumers the right to choose between watching startup photos, videos, or startup advertisements, but did not grant them the right to refuse to watch startup advertisements or other startup photos or videos, improperly limiting the scope of the consumer's right to choose. Therefore, this function cannot exempt or replace the statutory obligations of the business operator. Furthermore, the "Test Report" and "Expert Opinion" submitted by the appellee, Jiangsu Provincial Consumer Protection Committee, have already proven that playing startup advertisements lengthens the startup time, increasing the waiting time for consumers, and there is no technical obstacle to setting up a one-click close function while playing the startup advertisement. Consequently, even if the fact claimed by Lerong Zhixin Company — that due to technical reasons, the television needs a warm-up period upon startup, and not playing an advertisement would result in a black screen — were established, it cannot serve as a reason for refusing to set up a one-click close window. The startup advertisements loaded on the "LeTV," "Letv," and "Letv Super TV" brand smart televisions produced and sold by Lerong Zhixin Company only pop up a one-click close window in the final 5 seconds of playback, allowing consumers to choose to close the startup advertisement only then. This significantly reduces the consumer's experience of watching television and infringes upon the consumer's right to choose.

During the second instance, the appellant, Lerong Zhixin Company, argued that the startup advertisements set on the smart televisions it sold complied with industry standards, and the one-click close function also followed the provisions of the Advertising Law, granting consumers the right to choose. In response, the court held that the "Specification for Smart TV Startup Advertising Service" does not clearly stipulate how startup advertisements should set up a one-click close function to ensure the realization of consumer's right to choose, which does not mean that business operators can freely set up the one-click close function. It is not prohibited by law for industry associations to formulate industry standards for startup advertisements, but industry standards cannot be lower than legal standards. Business conduct, while complying with industry standards, must also comply with legal provisions and the general understanding of the broad consumer public. The existing evidence shows that the one-click close function set up by Lerong Zhixin Company does not meet the requirements of the Advertising Law and lacks immediacy. The court does not support Lerong Zhixin Company's defense. The first instance finding that Lerong Zhixin Company infringed upon the legitimate rights and interests of numerous unspecified consumers has factual and legal basis and is upheld.

From October 21, 2019, when the appellant, Lerong Zhixin Company, wrote to the appellee, Jiangsu Provincial Consumer Protection Committee, until the opening of the second instance trial in this case, over a year had passed. The company's commitment to the Jiangsu Provincial Consumer Protection Committee to improve startup advertisements and set up a one-click close window had, in fact, seen no substantive progress. The first instance considered that older models previously sold by Lerong Zhixin Company were subject to software and hardware technical limitations and required significant functional modifications. It did not impose a time limit for rectification on smart televisions already sold, only ordering Lerong Zhixin Company, from the date this judgment takes effect, to provide a one-click close function for the smart televisions it sold that contain startup advertisements, simultaneously with the playback of the startup advertisement. This has fully considered Lerong Zhixin Company's interests, reflects respect and tolerance for market entities, and is also upheld.

In summary, the appellant Lerong Zhixin Company's appeal claims and reasons are all untenable and are not supported. The Jiangsu High People's Court, in accordance with Article 29, Paragraph 3 of the *Law of the People's Republic of China on the Protection of Consumer Rights and Interests*, Article 44, Paragraph 2 of the *Advertising Law of the People's Republic of China*, and Article 170, Paragraph 1, Item 1 of the *Civil Procedure Law of the People's Republic of China*, on March 23, 2021, rendered the following judgment:

The appeal is dismissed, and the original judgment is affirmed.

This judgment is final.
